what_its_for: Larotrectinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain solid tumors (cancers) in adults and children. It works specifically for tumors that have a specific gene change called an 'NTRK gene fusion.' Your doctor will test your tumor to confirm you have this gene change before starting this medicine. It can be used for many different types of cancer as long as the NTRK gene fusion is present and the cancer has spread or cannot be removed with surgery.
how_to_take: Take larotrectinib by mouth (orally) with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or open them. If you are using the liquid (oral solution), use the measuring device provided with your medicine to measure the correct dose. Do not use a household spoon. Take it at the same time each day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body size (height and weight) and your kidney or liver health. The usual adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (every 12 hours). For children, the dose is usually calculated based on body surface area. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since your scheduled dose time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store larotrectinib capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Short trips to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) are okay. Store the oral liquid solution in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Throw away any unused liquid after 90 days of opening. Keep all medicine out of the reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of larotrectinib in your blood and cause more side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) as it can make larotrectinib less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with larotrectinib. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or have trouble with balance or coordination, as this medicine can cause these side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: dizziness, unsteadiness, or problems with balance and walking; memory problems, confusion, or difficulty speaking or understanding words; mood changes, depression, or anxiety; numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or feet; unusual fatigue or weakness; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or upper right belly pain; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or body aches; nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Larotrectinib may start working within the first few weeks of treatment, but it can take several months before you and your doctor see the full benefit. Response times vary from person to person. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans and tests. Do not stop taking this medicine even if you feel well unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not take larotrectinib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after your last dose, as the drug may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Females and Males: Women of childbearing age and male patients with female partners who could become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment. Children: This medicine can be used in children of any age, but dosing is carefully adjusted based on the child's body size. Liver or Kidney Problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
